web_evidence.title: Nicholas Sparks (author) Writing Styles in The Best of Me
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly identifies the novel as third-person omniscient and explains that viewpoint shifts among Amanda, Dawson, and minor characters occur at chapters or section breaks without changing grammatical person.

person_note: The base narration is third person, shifting focal attention among Dawson, Amanda, and other characters while retaining external he/she reference. Numerous Goodreads event passages independently show sustained third-person scene narration and interior access, agreeing with the authorized opening and the explicit whole-book POV description. First-person material in the quote set is dialogue, recollection, or Tuck's embedded letter rather than an autonomous first-person base section; the main limitation is that the authorized continuous excerpt covers only the opening, but the quote corpus and whole-book structural description remove material uncertainty. Quote audit: six nondiagnostic speech-beat or descriptive passages were conservatively changed to unmarked; sustained interior narration still supports THIRD.
